newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen higher after Tuesday rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen higher after Tuesday rally.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to higher Wednesday after yesterday's rally tied to keen paper buying and strength in the daily cash market in the western U.S.
"I expect it to rally some more. I don't see it turning around," said a New York futures broker.
In over-the-counter business, May California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted $14.60-14.70 a megawatt hour (MWh), while May Palo Verde (PV) $18.75-19.00.
On ACCESS, May COB finished with an offer at $14.60 against yesterday's close at $14.11, and May PV ended with a bid at $18.30 against Tuesday's settlement at $18.88.
On Tuesday, day-ahead power values in the West were running at $5-7 premium above May futures.

Firm swing natural gas prices, air-conditioning demand in the Southwest and significant number of plant outages throughout the West have contributed to the strength in the cash market, market sources said.

Cash power prices could begin to ease as the Southwest begins to cool today and some of the 7,000 megawatt (MW) thermal generating capacity which has been offline for repairs are set to return to service.
Two MW coal-fired units at the Jim Bridger generating complex in Wyoming may resume operation by today after being shut, market sources said.
Stormy conditions are expected to move across the West into the weekend with temperatures varying widely throughout the region.
Readings in the Northwest would average from seven degrees Fahrenheit above normal in the extreme northwest to seven degrees F below normal in the the southeast area.
In the Southwest, temperatures will average from five degrees F above normal in the far west to nine degrees F below normal in the extreme east.

Separately, Bonneville Power Administration told Reuters Tuesday that water flow through the 6,150 MW Grand Coulee Dam in Washington may be reduced to minimize the threat of downstream flooding, especially near Portland, Oregon.

Three large nuclear power units in the West are shut for refueling and maintenance: the 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 1 in Avila Beach, Calif.; the 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear power unit in San Clemente, Calif.; and the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Richland, Washington.
